title: the chakras as a map, not a claim (science seat)
hook: anatomy posters label organs; this old map writes letters on its petals
carry: the chakras as a map, not a claim (science seat)
tomorrow: a moon on the left, a sun on the right. what runs between?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the chakras as a map rose to the crown: a lotus of a thousand petals, and a meeting, not a switch. Today, a closer look at those petals.

Anatomy posters label things: thighbone, artery, nerve. The Sat-Cakra-Nirupana labels its map too, but strangely. Each lotus along the spine has letters of the Sanskrit alphabet set on its petals. At its center sits a shape and a seed sound, and inside, a god and a goddess. No one has ever drawn an organ like that. So why would a map of the body carry an alphabet?
screen: `ANATOMY POSTERS LABEL ORGANS.` → `THIS MAP WRITES LETTERS ON PETALS.` → `WHY AN ALPHABET?`

segments.voice: Because it isn't a map of the body's parts. It's a map of what the mind does on the way up. Every detail is something to hold: a shape to picture, a sound to say inwardly, a figure to honor, an order to follow. Letters belong on a map like that. Sound matters in this tradition: mantras are made of syllables, and each lotus here has a bija, a seed sound, at its center. So as attention climbs, it climbs through sound. Here's the line worth taking to dinner: the old map is drawn with an alphabet, not a scalpel. That one detail tells you what kind of map you're holding. A subway map isn't drawn to scale either. Its stations aren't evenly spaced, its lines aren't that straight, and nobody calls it false. It does one job, and does it well. Some modern writers have tried to line the lotuses up with glands or bundles of nerves. The old map doesn't need that to do its work, and it never asked for it. Read on its own terms, the puzzle solves itself. Letters on petals means this is a place for the mind to rest, and listen.
screen: `LETTERS ON EVERY PETAL.` · `A MAP OF WHAT THE MIND DOES.` · `BIJA: A SEED SOUND AT THE CENTER.` · `AN ALPHABET, NOT A SCALPEL.` · then, large: `A PLACE TO REST, AND LISTEN.`

segments.voice: On any scrap of paper, draw a small lotus with a few petals. On each petal write one letter, the first letter of someone or something you want to keep close, and put a dot in the middle. Rest your eyes on it, petal by petal, for the rest of the sit.
The chakras as a map: lotuses with letters on their petals and a seed sound at the center, drawn for the mind, not for the scalpel.
screen: `THE CHAKRAS AS A MAP — today's word`.

segments.voice: For the road: the chakras as a map, not a claim, drawn with an alphabet. Until tomorrow, then.
